findings.explanation: createSessionToken embeds an exp timestamp (line 142: exp: issuedAt + maxAgeMs) and the token is properly signed with HMAC-SHA256 (signValue, line 55) and verified with a constant-time comparison (safeEqualText, line 159) — signing is fine. But verifySessionToken (lines 149-181) never reads or compares payload.exp against the current time anywhere in the function. The only branch that returns reason 'expired_admin_session' (line 169-171) actually fires on `payload.v !== 1`, a version mismatch, not on real expiration — there is no code path that rejects an old-but-validly-signed token. As a result, once issued, an admin session token remains accepted forever (until SESSION_SECRET is rotated), regardless of the intended 8-hour TTL (DEFAULT_SESSION_TTL_MS, line 9) and regardless of the cookie's Max-Age, which only affects whether the browser resends it, not whether the server accepts it. A token captured via logs, a proxy, referrer leakage, or a browser/device compromise stays valid indefinitely, and logout (submitLogout, line 420) only clears the cookie client-side without any server-side revocation, so a copied token keeps working after the user logs out.
